subject: Re: Redwood demo + pricing discussion (ZenPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@zenpay.com>; Devon Lee <devon.lee@zenpay.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo + quick pricing questions

Hi Aisha / Devon —

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the walk-through of ZenPay's fraud detection flows and where you're thinking of embedding small LLM prompts for normalization and risk scoring. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can put together a tight cost/commit proposal: 

Recap (high level):
- Primary initial use case: transaction normalization + merchant risk scoring (low-latency, high-throughput).
- Expected Q4 pilot: ~50M tokens/month (inference tokens only), with production ramp to ~150-200M tokens/month within 6–9 months if latency & accuracy meet requirements.
- Peak qps requirement: ~120 concurrent requests, median response length ~150 tokens.

Asks to validate pricing:
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly token band for the pilot (best estimate, low/likely/high)?
2) What is the approximate monthly cloud and procurement approval threshold (e.g., do you need PO > $25k, > $50k, > $100k)?
3) Any constraints on contract term length (month-to-month vs 6/12 month commit)?

Ballpark from our side (so we're aligned on expectations):
- Pay-as-you-go typically sits at a higher $/1M-token unit. Commits buy down unit cost substantially.
- We'll prepare 3 options: no-commit (flexible), mid-commit (3–6 month), and enterprise commit (12+ months) with associated unit economics.

If you can reply with your best estimates on (1) and (2) above, I'll loop in Dylan and Rishi to draft a pricing worksheet and a short SOW for procurement.

Thanks — available for a quick 30-min follow-up this week if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@zenpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon.lee@zenpay.com>, procurement@zenpay.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo + quick pricing questions

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — that matches our notes. Quick answers below: 

1) Token band (pilot -> production):
- Pilot (Q4): low 30M / likely 50M / high 75M tokens/month
- Production (6–9 months): low 100M / likely 150M / high 200M tokens/month

2) Procurement thresholds / approvals:
- Small POs: up to $25k can be handled by engineering procurement.
- Mid-tier: $25k–$75k requires Procurement + Finance approval (turnaround ~2–3 weeks).
- > $75k requires Legal + Procurement + VP approvals (can trigger longer review).

3) Contract length: For pilots we prefer month-to-month or 3-month trial with option to commit. For enterprise pricing/discounts we can commit to 6–12 months but procurement will insist on an SOW and standard security clauses.

One more data point: our internal target unit economics for tooling/infra is around $500–$900 per 1M tokens (we're benchmarking against previous vendors). If you can hit numbers in that band with a reasonable commit, we can fast-track.

Looping in Devon (finance) and procurement for any clarifying Qs.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product, ZenPay
aisha.khan@zenpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ZenPay numbers — wants $500–$900/1M target; procurement thresholds noted

Team — forwarding Aisha's reply (see below). Key points: 50M pilot likely, scale to 150–200M; procurement signoff bands: <=$25k, $25–$75k, >$75k; target unit economics $500–$900/1M.

Proposed quick pricing framework to align internally before we send official worksheet: 
- Option A (pay-as-you-go): $1,500 / 1M tokens (no commit) — good for short pilot but above their target.
- Option B (6-month commit): commit to 100M tokens/month average, unit cost $900 / 1M tokens — fits upper end of their target; estimated monthly spend ~ $90k at 100M.
- Option C (12-month enterprise commit): commit to 200M tokens/month, unit cost $700 / 1M tokens — fits comfortably; estimated monthly spend ~ $140k at 200M.

Procurement gating notes: 
- If their procurement requires PO > $25k handled by procurement, we should expect a 2–3 week lead for mid-tier approvals.
- Anything > $75k likely needs Legal review; coordinate with SE + Legal early.

Ask: Can we tighten the committed price ranges or add a stepped discount band (e.g., 0–50M @ $1,100; 50–150M @ $850; 150M+ @ $700)? That gives them a smoother ramp and makes approvals easier. Also want to confirm whether we can include a 30-day exit clause for pilot months to reduce procurement friction.

Quick replies appreciated — I'd like to send the external worksheet + SOW by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa
